skill.name: qryma-search
skill.description: Search the web through the Qryma API and return results in Markdown, raw JSON, or Brave-style formats. The skill supports language, result count, pagination, safe search, and fulltext or snippet modes.
skill.summary: Run Qryma-powered web searches with configurable result formats and search options.
skill.author: qryma-ai

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate Qryma web-search wrapper, but it performs real network egress and handles API credentials. Confirmed risks include API key loading from environment and .env files, transmission of the key in an outbound header, a configurable endpoint that can redirect credentials, and documentation that encourages sharing keys with an AI assistant.

remediation.issue: Documentation encourages users to send QRYMA_API_KEY to an AI assistant.
remediation.suggestion: Replace those instructions with manual setup steps that never ask users to paste real secrets into chat prompts or tool transcripts.

remediation.issue: The endpoint can be overridden while the X-Api-Key header is sent to the selected endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict endpoint overrides to trusted hosts, require explicit confirmation for custom endpoints, or omit credentials when the endpoint is not the official Qryma API.

remediation.issue: The skill automatically reads .env and ~/.qryma/.env for credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicit credential path or platform secret store, document file permission requirements, and avoid scanning hidden home-directory files by default.

remediation.issue: API keys can be passed on the command line or event payload.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment or managed secret injection and warn users that command-line secrets may appear in shell history, process lists, or logs.

remediation.issue: Search queries are sent to an external API.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear privacy documentation explaining that queries and request metadata are transmitted to Qryma during use.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Sharing Guidance Risks Secret Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: README.md and SKILL.md tell users to ask an AI assistant to configure QRYMA_API_KEY. If users replace the placeholder with a real key, the secret can be stored in chat logs, tool transcripts, or third-party systems.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly connects QRYMA_API_KEY setup with asking an AI assistant to configure it. This is a clear social-engineering risk for credential exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Configurable Endpoint Can Receive API Key
semantic_findings.description: scripts/search_core.py loads QRYMA_ENDPOINT from the environment or .env files, then sends self.api_key in the X-Api-Key header to that endpoint. A modified endpoint can receive both user queries and the API key.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data flow is visible in the source: endpoint configuration is loaded before the request is built, and the API key is attached to the request headers.

content.value_statement: Finding current web information can be slow when an assistant has no search path. This skill sends queries to Qryma and returns structured or readable results.
actual_capabilities: Runs web searches through the Qryma Search API.
Accepts query, result count, language, pagination, safe search, and mode options.
Returns results in Markdown, raw structured output, or Brave-style format.
Loads the API key from an argument, environment variable, or .env file.
Supports command-line execution and a platform handler entry point.
limitations: Requires a valid QRYMA_API_KEY before searches can run.
Sends search queries and the API key to an external Qryma endpoint.
Does not verify source quality or fact-check returned pages.
Result freshness and coverage depend on the Qryma service.

best_practices: Use a managed secret store or protected environment variable for QRYMA_API_KEY.
Ask focused search questions and request source links for later review.
Use Markdown output for reading and structured output for downstream processing.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into chat prompts or shared transcripts.
Do not use this skill for private or regulated queries without reviewing Qryma data handling.
Do not trust search snippets as verified facts without checking the linked sources.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires QRYMA_API_KEY to call the Qryma Search API.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: It supports Markdown, raw structured output, and a Brave-style result format.

faq.question: Can I change the search language?
faq.answer: Yes. The language option can be set when running a search.

faq.question: Does it run fully offline?
faq.answer: No. It sends requests to a Qryma search endpoint.

faq.question: Can I use a custom endpoint?
faq.answer: The code supports QRYMA_ENDPOINT, but custom endpoints can receive the API key.

faq.question: Should I paste my API key into an assistant chat?
faq.answer: No. Configure the key through a protected secret store or local environment setting.
